chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl, from his father Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who performs the first prayer, then performs a supererogatory prayer, and the time of ʿaṣr comes upon him before he finishes his nāfilah: should he delay ʿaṣr until after his nāfilah, or perform the nāfilah after ʿaṣr, or postpone it until he performs it at the end of its time?
He said: He should perform ʿaṣr and make up his nāfilah on another day.

The correct way of understanding this report is that if he were to pray at the end of its time, he would have approached the setting of the sun, and that is a time in which prayer is disliked, as we have explained. This too is to be understood in accordance with what we mentioned regarding recommendation.

key_terms.آخِرِ وَقْتٍ: the end portion of the designated prayer time
key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةَ الشَّمْسِ: the setting or disappearance of the sun
key_terms.نَافِلَتِهِ: his recommended prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the prescribed time of the ʿaṣr prayer
key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up what was missed at a later time

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if the time of ʿaṣr enters while he is still performing a nāfilah prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who is engaged in a nāfilah prayer when the time of ʿaṣr arrives. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the obligatory ʿaṣr prayer should take precedence, while the missed nāfilah may be made up on another day, especially since delaying until near sunset enters a disliked time for prayer.
